Definition: properly, the (outer) wall side; hence, exterior; figuratively, secular (as opposed to sacred)
BiblicalUsage: Chiytsown is the outer side, the exterior, and it marks the boundary between the holy and the common. The temple has carvings in the inner house and the outer, the king's entry is taken away from the outer way, Haman waits in the outward court, and Ezekiel measures the outward court of the new temple.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the outer places matter because they are where ordinary people stand before God, and He has always made room there. I hold that the God who dwells in the inner place still meets His people in the outer court.
